nodes.name: Every new product repeats a familiar setup. Someone writes…
nodes.text: Every new product repeats a familiar setup. Someone writes down how the code is organized. Someone else collects the logo files, the brand colors, the naming rules and the deployment notes. A month later, half of it lives in a chat thread and the other half in a file nobody is sure is current.

nodes.name: Agents make this more visible, not less. An agent session…
nodes.text: Agents make this more visible, not less. An agent session starts with no memory of the last one. It needs to be told the same things each time, and when the guidance is scattered, it either asks again or guesses. Both cost time, and guessing costs trust.

nodes.name: NullDull exists to remove that repetition. We provide…
nodes.text: NullDull exists to remove that repetition. We provide tools for startups to start fast, built so that the people on a team and the agents working for them use the same context, the same configuration and the same permissions.

nodes.name: “Agent-first” is a design constraint, not a slogan. Every…
nodes.text: “Agent-first” is a design constraint, not a slogan. Every implemented capability is meant to be available through the interface, the HTTP API, the MCP server and the CLI, with the same rules behind each. There is no private shortcut for the browser and no special back door for agents.

nodes.name: That matters because a team rarely uses one tool. One…
nodes.text: That matters because a team rarely uses one tool. One person works in the browser. Another works through Codex or Claude Code. NullDull’s in-app agent, Null, works inside the console. All of them read the same files and hit the same version checks. When an agent proposes a change, it goes through the same review a person’s change would.

nodes.name: Usable by people means the interface is not an…
nodes.text: Usable by people means the interface is not an afterthought. Decisions such as approving a sensitive change, granting access to a secret or publishing a page stay in the browser, where a person makes them deliberately.

nodes.name: A startup’s product is rarely one repository. It might…
nodes.text: A startup’s product is rarely one repository. It might have a web app, a shared core, iOS and Android apps and a browser extension. Those projects share a product name, a brand and a set of decisions, but each also has rules of its own.

nodes.name: NullDull models that directly. A **workspace** is the…
nodes.text: NullDull models that directly. A **workspace** is the organization: members, teams and organization-wide resources. Most teams organize it as projects. Agencies and companies with several products can turn on **Products** in workspace settings and group projects under each product. A **project** is a component or workstream such as web or iOS, with its own files and configuration.

nodes.name: The result is shared product context with project-specific…
nodes.text: The result is shared product context with project-specific control. Product-wide guidance lives once, at the product. Each project keeps the instructions that only apply to it. No repository needs its own workspace, and nothing needs to be copied just to be visible somewhere else.

nodes.name: Shared context is only useful if people trust where it…
nodes.text: Shared context is only useful if people trust where it goes. NullDull treats access as something you can read and explain. Senior and Junior are roles on a resource: the same person can edit one file directly and propose changes to another. Grid has its own reader, editor and manager roles. Secrets have their own grants.

nodes.name: Agent connections are explicit too. When you connect an…
nodes.text: Agent connections are explicit too. When you connect an agent, you approve one workspace and choose what it may do in Memory, and separately whether it may touch Grid or Secrets. A Memory grant never silently opens another product, and a connection can be changed or revoked from Settings at any time.

nodes.name: Memory is available in invite-only early access. Grid is…
nodes.text: Memory is available in invite-only early access. Grid is in early access, with its own consent. Client SDKs for six languages and the Grid packages for npm are published as early access releases. Locale, for translation, and Tasks, for shared work by people and agents, are in early access. Feedbacks comes later, followed by further products we describe on the roadmap.

nodes.name: Early access is invite-only and activated with a one-time…
nodes.text: Early access is invite-only and activated with a one-time early access code. It includes the suite free, needs no payment method and does not silently turn into a paid subscription. If you are on the waiting list, we’ll be in touch when access is ready; we don’t promise a date.
